original_question: Let F_*(n) denote a partial billiard complexity obtained by coding only orbit families satisfying additional restrictions; for example, periodic complexity counts periodic-orbit codes. Find nontrivial explicit bounds on such partial billiard complexities for a general polygon.
target_in_paper: Section 5.4, Problem 14: "Find nontrivial, explicit bounds on partial billiard complexities for the general polygon," together with the immediately preceding definitions of the code w(gamma), the sets W_n(P), the full complexity F(n), and the partial complexities F_*(n).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's target as a coding-based partial/conditional complexity question for polygonal billiards, keeps the scope at general polygons, and asks for nontrivial explicit bounds rather than only asymptotic existence results. It also correctly treats periodic complexity as an example rather than replacing the whole problem by a narrower periodic-orbit question.
missing_details: The paper first fixes a polygon P and uses its sides as the coding alphabet A = {a, b, c, ...}.
A finite billiard orbit gamma is encoded by the word w(gamma) obtained by recording the successive sides of P that gamma hits.
The combinatorial length of gamma is the number of letters in w(gamma), and W_n(P) denotes the set of codes of all billiard orbits of exact combinatorial length n.
The full complexity is F(n) = sum_{k <= n} |W_k(P)|; a partial complexity F_*(n) is any analogous counting function obtained after imposing additional restrictions on the family of coded orbits.
F_*(n) is therefore not one fixed canonical function in the paper: the restriction defining it must be specified as part of the question.
The official formulation asks for both upper and lower bounds, and requires them to be explicit and nontrivial.
The paper notes that in Problem 14 the phrase "general polygon" may be replaced by "irrational polygon".
The periodic example is only an informal special-case pointer to Problem 11; the official Problem 14 itself is broader and is not limited to periodic-orbit codes.
refined_question: Let P be a polygon with side alphabet A = {a, b, c, ...}. For a finite billiard orbit gamma in P, let w(gamma) be the word recording the successive sides of P hit by gamma, let the combinatorial length of gamma be the number of letters in w(gamma), and let W_n(P) be the set of codes of all billiard orbits of combinatorial length n. Define the full billiard complexity by F(n) = sum_{k <= n} |W_k(P)|, and let F_*(n) denote any conditional (partial) complexity obtained by imposing a specified additional restriction on the family of coded billiard orbits (for example, the periodic case referred to via Problem 11). Find nontrivial explicit upper and lower bounds for F_*(n) for a general polygon P (as noted in the paper, one may replace "general polygon" by "irrational polygon").
justification: The draft is aiming almost verbatim at Problem 14, not at a broader neighboring statement. In Section 5.4 the paper first introduces the side-coding of finite billiard orbits, defines W_n(P), the full complexity F(n), and the restricted/partial complexities F_*(n), and then states Problem 14 in essentially the same words as the draft. The same paragraph says that Problem 11 is only a special case of this more general partial-complexity question, while Conjecture 1 is presented afterward merely to make the problem more concrete for the full complexity F, not to replace Problem 14. The main incompleteness in the draft is therefore not its scope but the omission of the coding conventions, the exact counting setup, and the paper's upper-and-lower-bound wording.
